content:
- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.90) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment drops sharply (especially <0.30) — model misses downward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to recent highs/lows, fails to smoothly transition toward historical averages.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often peaks 1–2 days after true price turns, especially in bearish sentiment.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model overweights momentum and ignores volatility tail risks.
- When sentiment is low and price is falling, model underweights the decline, leading to delayed correction.
- Model tends to overcorrect after sharp spikes — forecasts drop too aggressively after peaks, missing the “rebound” phase.
- Sentiment history should be weighted more heavily in early forecast windows — model underweights sentiment in first 5–7 days of horizon.
